questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The man told me who I was to blame him.
options_en: The man said to me, "Who are you to blame me?"
The man said to me, "Who you are to blame me?"
The man said to me, "Who am I to blame you?"
The man said to me," Who were you to blame me?"
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc in Indirect Speech is changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

For example:

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past Simple. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the Present Simple.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

· The reporting verb 'told' is changed into 'said to'.

· The pronouns 'I' and 'him' are changed into 'you' and 'me' respectively.

· The verb 'was' (past simple) is changed into 'are' (present simple).

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The man said to me, "Who are you to blame me?"

·For example:

o Kindly, wash the dishes as soon as possible. (Active)

·Therefore, the correct answer is:You are requested to submit the assignment on time.

If the sentence is in Simple Past, the form of tense doesn't change when two actions happened simultaneously.

For example:

Rekha said, "I cooked the food and he set up the table." (Direct Speech)

Rekha said that she cooked the food and he set up the table. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

 The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

 The pronouns 'I' and 'me' are changed into 'he' and 'him' respectively.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Rakesh told me that he cleaned the house and he helped him with the task.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The dining room is located interior with the living room, creating a cosy and integrated space for family gatherings.
questions.solution_en:
According to the rule, the adjectives that end in 'ior' like 'senior, junior, interior, exterior, etc.' are followed by 'to'. So, 'interior to' is the correct phrase and not 'interior with'.

The correct sentence is - "The dining room is located interior to the living room, creating a cosy and integrated space for family gatherings."

Hence, option (d) is correct.

NOTE/-

Adjectives: Words which are used with a noun/pronoun to describe or point out, the person, animal, place, or thing which the noun names, or to tell the number or quantity, are called Adjectives.

questions.q_en:
Fill in the blanks with the correct pair of words.

I saw your ___ playing outside in the ___ this afternoon.
questions.solution_en:
The given sentence talks about the speaker seeing a person playing outside in the afternoon. Both blanks require a noun as the first blank is preceded by a possessive determiner (your) and the second blank is preceded by the definite article 'the'. 'Son' means one's male offspring and 'sun' means the star which is the centre of the solar system. Among the given options, 'son' and 'sun' fit in the blanks respectively as their usage conveys that the speaker saw a person's kid playing in the sunlight this afternoon. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate homophone of the underlined word to fill in the blank.

The bookstore had a huge sale on musical books, so he bought one to learn the ______ on his guitar.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate homophone of the underlined word to fill in the blank is 'scale'. This word means an arrangement of the notes in any system of music in ascending or descending order of pitch. The other options are not suitable homophones of 'sale', which means a period during which a shop or dealer sells goods at reduced prices. 'Sail' means a piece of material extended on a mast to catch the wind and propel a boat or ship or other vessel, 'gale' means a very strong wind, and 'seal' means a marine mammal or a device that prevents leakage.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.
